correctness.rationale: The real-space hypotheses and the actual norm agree exactly with equation (24). Appendix A defines Y on c0 by the closed convex hull of Gamma={+/-e1+/-en:n>=2} and D={y in B_c0:y1=0}; (1/2)B_c0 is contained in B_Y contained in B_c0, so the canonical coordinate vectors belong to Y. Taking the dual support function gives max(sum_{n>=2}|xn|,|x1|+max_{n>=2}|xn|). The strong-uniqueness premise is also verified from the source proof: (e1*+2en*)/3 exposes e1+en, with other generators bounded by 2/3, yielding ||z-(e1+en)||<=6(1-<x_n,z>); the signed variants span Y. Lemma 2.3 puts them in every concrete predual, and Fact 2.2 rules out proper nesting. For every nonempty I, deleting coordinates decreases both norm terms and P_I fixes a nonzero vector, hence ||P_I||=1. X_I is the intersection of kernels of the e_n in Y for n outside I, hence weak-star closed. For infinite I omitting 1 the restricted norm is exactly the l1 norm; for infinite I containing 1, a bijection of its infinite tail transports equation (24) isometrically. l1 has nonisometric isometric preduals c0 and c: their dual measures are countable l1, whereas c has extreme points in its unit ball and c0 does not. The continuum multiplicities follow from infinite subsets of a countable tail. Deleting {1,...,k} or {2,...,k+1} removes exactly k coordinates and gives the two codimension-k outcomes. The empty projection is excluded; no infinite-dimensional predual dichotomy is asserted for finite I or for non-coordinate subspaces. No numerical or exhaustive experiment is needed.
